newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan denies coastguard boarded HK protest boat.
newsitem.headline: Japan denies coastguard boarded HK protest boat.

text.p: The Japanese coastguard denied a Taiwanese radio report on Monday that it boarded a Hong Kong boat and prepared to arrest activists challenging Tokyo's claim to an East China Sea island chain.

A spokesman for the coastguard, Japan's Maritime Safety Agency, said there were no reports that coastguard officials had boarded the Protect-the-Diaoyus boat from Hong Kong or any other protest boats.
"We have no reports that our men boarded any boats, including this Hong Kong vessel," the spokesman told Reuters.
He said at about noon (0300 GMT) the Hong Kong ship sailed into Japan's 12-nautical mile territorial waters around the chain of islands, called the Senkakus in Japanese and the Diaoyus in Chinese.
Taiwan state radio reported that Japanese coastguards had boarded the Protect-the-Diaoyus boat and planned to arrest activists on it.
The 100-tonne Protect-the-Diaoyus vessel was leading a 20-strong flotilla from Taiwan and Hong Kong that is challenging Japan's sovereignty over the island chain.
